decision: tad in Rust: tables declared as data (after Frictionless Table Schema); one tool - check, canonical form, row edits with a check, documents rendered from data; proven equal to the Python version on all four repositories (same verdicts, same documents) before any switch; delivered by the package conveyor instead of vendored; ocoeco's shapes become a tad declaration. The tool is delivered by the package conveyor (for CI and machines); the library is taken as a Rhizoid cutting where a project builds on it (ocoeco) - as tad's own path already says, a rhizcut in every repository.
why: The author: tad stays general and Python leaves. The four schemas need no database engine: their 41 tables use only patterns, allowed values, required fields and one list column.
rejected: Rust bindings to DuckDB keeping schema.sql (a database engine to validate text); Dolt (a separate store); keeping the vendored copies.
